shortAnswer: If KDP says "Barcode Area Contains Text," clear the lower-right area of the back cover where Amazon places its barcode. Move text, logos, QR codes, decorative frames, and important artwork away from that reserved box, then re-export and check the cover in Previewer.

faqs.question: Where does Amazon place the barcode on paperback covers?
faqs.answer: For most paperback covers, Amazon KDP places the barcode in the lower-right area of the back cover. The exact reserved area should be checked on the latest KDP cover template for your trim size, page count, and setup.

faqs.question: Can I remove the KDP barcode?
faqs.answer: Most paperback books need a barcode for printing and distribution. If you let KDP assign or place the barcode, you should leave the reserved barcode area clear on the back cover.

faqs.question: Can artwork go behind the barcode?
faqs.answer: Simple background colors or subtle textures can usually continue behind the barcode area, but important text, logos, QR codes, detailed illustrations, or high-contrast patterns should not sit there.

faqs.question: Why did KDP suddenly add a white barcode box?
faqs.answer: KDP adds a white barcode box when it needs a readable barcode on the printed back cover. If your design has content in that area, the white box can cover it or trigger a warning.

faqs.question: How much space should I leave for the barcode?
faqs.answer: Use the barcode box shown in the latest KDP cover template and leave extra padding around it. Do not guess from memory, because the safest area can vary by trim size and template.

faqs.question: Can Canva templates cause barcode problems?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many Canva templates are made for visual appeal and do not include the KDP barcode safe zone. Import the KDP template into Canva as a locked guide layer and design around it.

faqs.question: Does hardcover KDP use the same barcode placement?
faqs.answer: Hardcover layouts can use different templates and production zones. Always download the correct KDP template for the exact format, trim size, binding, page count, and paper settings.

faqs.question: Can I put social media handles near the barcode?
faqs.answer: Avoid putting social handles, websites, QR codes, or calls to action near the lower-right back cover. Move them higher or toward the left so they do not overlap the barcode box.

faqs.question: Will KDP reject my book if text overlaps the barcode?
faqs.answer: KDP can warn or reject the cover if important content overlaps the barcode area. Even if it passes, the printed barcode box may cover your design, so it is best to fix the layout before publishing.

content:
If Amazon KDP says "Barcode Area Contains Text," it means the automatic barcode box on the back cover overlaps text, logos, patterns, QR codes, or important graphics in your design. The cover may have looked perfectly fine in Canva, Photoshop, Affinity, or Illustrator, but KDP is checking the production layout, not just the artwork.

This warning is common because the back cover feels like usable design space until KDP places the barcode. Then a white barcode box suddenly appears in the lower-right corner and covers part of the design. For paperback books, this area must stay visually clear enough for Amazon to print and scan the barcode reliably.

KDP adds a barcode automatically for many paperback books because the printed book needs identification for manufacturing, distribution, and retail handling. If the reserved barcode zone contains important content, KDP may warn you, reject the cover, or cover your artwork with a white barcode box in Previewer.

The "Barcode Area Contains Text" warning is especially common for Canva users, coloring book creators, journal makers, puzzle book publishers, and low-content book designers. These covers often use decorative borders, full-page patterns, social handles, QR codes, or call-to-action text near the bottom-right back cover. That is exactly where the barcode usually needs to go.

## What Is the KDP Barcode Area?

The KDP barcode area is a reserved region on the back cover where Amazon can place the printed barcode. It is not a decorative design element. It is a production requirement.

For most paperback covers, Amazon places the barcode automatically if you do not supply your own approved barcode in the correct way. The barcode usually appears as black barcode lines inside a white box. That white box may cover anything underneath it.

The barcode area is used for printing and distribution. It helps Amazon identify and process the physical book. Because the barcode must remain readable, KDP does not want text, logos, QR codes, detailed illustrations, or busy patterns competing with it.

Important elements inside this zone may become unreadable. A website URL could disappear behind the white box. A logo could be cut in half. A decorative frame could make the barcode area look messy. A QR code could sit too close to Amazon's barcode and create a confusing back cover.

The barcode area is not optional for most paperback books. You can design around it, but you should not pretend it is not there.

## Where Is the Barcode Located on a Paperback Cover?

On a paperback cover, the barcode is usually placed in the lower-right corner of the back cover. Remember that a print cover is a full wraparound PDF: back cover on the left, spine in the middle, front cover on the right. The barcode belongs on the back cover panel, not the front cover.

The exact placement depends on the KDP template for your trim size, page count, paper type, and format. It can shift slightly based on the template. That is why you should not rely on a screenshot from another book or a template from a previous project.

Many beginners design the full back cover as if every inch is available. They place blurbs, subtitles, author bios, logos, social handles, decorative frames, and QR codes anywhere that looks balanced. Visually, that can look good. Technically, the lower-right back cover needs to reserve space for the barcode.

The safest approach is to download the latest KDP cover template for the exact book setup and keep the barcode zone visible while designing.

## Why This Warning Happens

The warning appears when KDP detects content inside or too close to the barcode region. The content may be obvious text, or it may be something you did not think of as "text."

### Subtitle or Blurb Text Overlaps the Barcode Area

Back cover blurbs often run too low. If the final paragraph, subtitle, review quote, or series tagline reaches the lower-right corner, KDP may flag it. Even small text can trigger the warning because the barcode box needs a clean readable area.

### Author Logo Placed Too Low

Many authors put a logo, publisher mark, or imprint logo at the bottom of the back cover. That can work if it sits away from the barcode zone, but it often lands exactly where KDP places the barcode.

### QR Codes Inside the Barcode Region

QR codes are a common trigger. A QR code is scannable graphic information, and it should not compete with Amazon's barcode. Put QR codes away from the lower-right back cover, and leave breathing room around both codes.

### Decorative Borders Enter the Barcode Box

Coloring books, journals, puzzle books, and workbooks often use borders. If a border crosses the lower-right barcode zone, KDP may treat it as a design element inside the barcode area. A frame that looks harmless can still interfere with the barcode box.

### Patterns and Textures Become Unreadable

Subtle texture is usually less risky than text, but busy patterns can still look bad when covered by a white barcode box. If the texture is high contrast or contains letters, symbols, numbers, or small repeated shapes, it can create a messy barcode area.

### Full-Black Artwork Conflicts With the White Barcode Box

If your entire back cover is black or dark, KDP may place a white barcode box on top. That is normal, but it can look abrupt. You may want to design a simple intentional light area for the barcode instead of letting it appear as an afterthought.

### Canva Templates Ignore the Barcode Area

Many Canva templates are visually attractive but not technically prepared for KDP. They may include bottom-corner text, full-frame borders, or decorative elements where the barcode needs to sit. A template can be pretty and still be unsafe for print production.

### Designing for Aesthetics Without Technical Safe Zones

The back cover is both a design surface and a production file. If you only design for visual balance, you can accidentally place important information in print zones that Amazon reserves for trimming, barcode placement, or manufacturing variation. Use the [safe area glossary](/glossary/safe-area) and [printable area glossary](/glossary/printable-area) concepts while composing the cover.

## The Most Common Beginner Mistake

The most common beginner mistake is thinking the entire back cover is usable space.

It is understandable. In Canva or Photoshop, the back cover looks like a blank rectangle. The bottom-right corner may feel like the perfect place for a website, Instagram handle, QR code, publisher logo, or small call to action. But KDP reserves that area automatically.

For example, a coloring book creator might place "Follow us for free coloring pages" in the bottom-right corner of the back cover. In the design file, it looks neat and balanced. After upload, KDP adds a white barcode box in that same corner. Now the text is covered, the design looks broken, and KDP may show a barcode warning.

The fix is not to fight the barcode. The fix is to plan for it from the beginning.

## How Big Is the KDP Barcode Area?

The safest answer is: use the barcode area shown on the latest KDP cover template for your book.

Authors often want one universal measurement, but guessing is risky. Barcode placement can depend on trim size, cover template, and print setup. KDP's template gives you the exact production guide for the current book configuration.

As a practical layout habit, leave more space than the barcode box itself. Give the barcode zone extra padding. Do not place text, logos, QR codes, or important illustrations right against the edge of the reserved area.

Do not rely on a manual guess copied from an old project. If you changed trim size, page count, paper type, binding type, or cover dimensions, download a fresh template. That advice also helps avoid broader cover-size issues like the [KDP cover size does not match interior warning](/blog/kdp-cover-size-does-not-match-interior).

## Step-by-Step Fix Workflow

### Step 1: Download the Latest KDP Cover Template

Go back to your current KDP book setup and generate a fresh cover template using the exact trim size, page count, ink type, paper type, and binding settings. Do not use an old template from a previous version of the book.

The template is your production map. It shows where the back cover, spine, front cover, bleed, trim, safe area, and barcode zone belong.

### Step 2: Locate the Barcode Zone

Open the template and find the barcode area on the back cover. It is usually near the lower-right corner of the back cover panel. Make sure you are looking at the back cover, not the front cover.

If your design tool lets you create guides, mark the barcode box clearly.

### Step 3: Move All Text and Logos Away

Move author logos, publisher marks, website URLs, social handles, QR codes, review text, and calls to action away from the barcode zone. Do not merely nudge them one or two pixels. Give the barcode room to breathe.

If the back cover starts to feel unbalanced, move the content upward or to the left instead of crowding the bottom-right corner.

### Step 4: Extend Background Graphics Safely Behind the Barcode

Background color, subtle texture, or simple artwork can usually continue behind the barcode zone. The key word is background. Important details should not live there.

If your background is dark, consider creating a deliberate quiet area for the barcode so the white barcode box does not feel accidental.

### Step 5: Keep Critical Information Outside the Reserved Box

Anything the reader needs to read or recognize should stay outside the barcode box and its padding. That includes title repeats, subtitles, author names, series marks, QR codes, logos, ISBN text, prices, and website addresses.

### Step 6: Re-Export the Cover PDF

Export a fresh print-ready PDF. Keep the correct full cover dimensions, include bleed if needed, and avoid extra crop marks or printer marks unless your workflow specifically requires them.

If the export settings change the page size, KDP may show a different warning. Use a [KDP cover checker](/tools/kdp-cover-checker) before uploading again.

### Step 7: Upload Again to KDP Previewer

Upload the corrected cover and open Previewer. Look at the lower-right back cover. Confirm that the barcode box no longer covers important content and that no warning remains.

Before uploading your paperback again, run your full cover through [KDPPreflight](/tools/kdp-cover-checker) to detect barcode conflicts, trim issues, bleed problems, and unsafe text placement before Amazon KDP rejects the file.

## Canva Fix Workflow

Canva users commonly run into barcode warnings because many templates are built for visual composition, not KDP production. A Canva design can look beautiful and still ignore the barcode safe zone.

Start by downloading the KDP cover template for your exact book. Upload the template into Canva and place it on top of your design as a guide layer. Resize it carefully so it matches the full cover dimensions. Then lower the transparency enough to see your design beneath it.

Lock the guide layer. This matters. If the KDP template moves while you design, the barcode guide becomes unreliable.

Keep all text outside the barcode area. This includes tiny text, social handles, website URLs, brand names, and QR codes. If you are designing a journal, puzzle book, coloring book, or workbook, also watch decorative frames and repeated patterns near the bottom-right back cover.

Maintain bleed correctly. Do not shrink the entire cover inward to avoid the barcode. Background artwork should still extend to the bleed edge when needed. The fix is to move important elements, not to create a random white border around the design.

When exporting, use PDF Print. Avoid accidentally flattening the barcode guide into the final artwork. Before export, hide or delete the KDP template guide layer unless your workflow requires otherwise. The guide is for you, not part of the final cover.

After export, confirm the final PDF dimensions if possible. If Canva added extra margins or exported the wrong size, fix that before uploading to KDP.

After you adjust the Canva layout, use [KDPPreflight](/tools/kdp-cover-checker) to check the exported PDF, not just the Canva canvas preview.

## Photoshop, Affinity, and Illustrator Workflow

In Photoshop, Affinity, or Illustrator, build a technical guide layer before you design the final back cover.

Use rulers and guides for the full wraparound cover. Mark the back cover, spine, front cover, bleed, trim, safe area, and barcode box. Lock the technical guide layer so it cannot shift accidentally.

Keep decorative borders away from the barcode box. If your design uses frames, rules, corner ornaments, or repeated icons, make sure they do not cross into the barcode reserve. A border may look like background, but KDP can still treat it as content in the barcode area.

Avoid exporting crop marks into the final PDF unless your specific KDP workflow calls for them. Extra marks can create other technical problems or make the file dimensions harder to diagnose. After any export, verify the PDF page dimensions match your expected cover size before reuploading.

Before exporting, turn off template overlays that should not print. Keep only the final artwork. Then inspect the back cover composition one more time with the guide layer visible in your source file.

## Can Artwork Go Behind the Barcode?

Yes, but with limits.

Background colors can extend behind the barcode area. Subtle paper texture, soft gradients, or low-contrast artwork can also be okay. KDP will usually place the barcode box over the area anyway.

What should not go behind the barcode is important information. Do not place small typography, logos, QR codes, social media handles, pricing, ISBN text, important illustrations, or detailed patterns inside the reserved zone.

Safe examples:

- solid background color
- subtle paper texture
- low-contrast background pattern
- simple color field that can be covered cleanly

Unsafe examples:

- important illustrations
- small typography
- author logos
- website URLs
- social handles
- QR codes
- decorative frames crossing through the barcode box

The best test is simple: if the barcode box covered this area completely, would the cover still make sense? If the answer is no, move the content.

## Best Back Cover Layout Practices

Plan the barcode area early, not after the cover is finished.

Keep the bottom-right back cover visually simple. Place blurbs higher. Put author bios, websites, and social handles away from the barcode area. Leave breathing room so the barcode feels like part of the production layout instead of a sticker covering the design.

For coloring books, avoid placing sample thumbnails or "bonus pages" text in the barcode corner. For journals and low-content books, be careful with full-page frames that run around the back cover. For puzzle books, keep difficulty labels, QR solution links, and website URLs out of the lower-right area.

If your back cover feels empty after clearing the barcode area, balance the composition with spacing, not clutter. A clean back cover often looks more professional than one packed with small elements.

## Common Barcode Area Mistakes

### Placing ISBN Text Inside the Barcode Box

Do not add extra ISBN text inside the barcode zone unless your exact barcode workflow requires it. KDP's automatic barcode handles the production need.

### Decorative Frames Crossing the Barcode Area

Frames are common on journals and coloring books. Keep them away from the reserved box or break the frame before it enters the barcode zone.

### Website or Social Handles Too Low

Bottom text feels natural, but the lower-right back cover is risky. Move social handles higher or place them toward the lower-left with enough clearance.

### Full-Page Back-Cover Artwork Conflicts

If the back cover is a full illustration, decide which part can safely be covered by the barcode box. Do not put a character face, important object, or text in that spot.

### Exporting the Wrong Template Version

If you resized the cover or changed trim size, the old barcode guide may no longer match. Download a new template.

### Forgetting Barcode Safe Area After Resizing

When you resize a cover, guides can drift or scale incorrectly. Re-check the barcode box after every major size change.

## How to Prevent This Problem Before Uploading

Start with the KDP template. Keep the guide visible while designing. Lock the guide layer so it cannot move. Build the back cover around the barcode area from the beginning.

Review the back cover carefully before export. Look specifically at the lower-right area. Ask whether any important text, logo, QR code, border, or detailed illustration would be covered by a white barcode box.

Test upload before publishing day. Do not wait until the final deadline to discover a barcode warning. A quick Previewer check can save a stressful round of emergency edits.

Finally, use preflight checking tools before KDP upload. KDPPreflight can help you catch barcode conflicts alongside trim, bleed, spine, and unsafe text placement issues.

## Quick Checklist Before Uploading Again

- Barcode area is clear
- Important text moved away
- Logos outside barcode box
- Decorative borders do not overlap barcode
- Back cover still balanced visually
- PDF exported correctly
- Correct KDP template used
- Bleed and background still correct

## FAQ

### Where does Amazon place the barcode on paperback covers?

Amazon KDP usually places the barcode in the lower-right area of the back cover. Use the latest KDP cover template for your exact book setup to confirm the exact reserved zone.

### Can I remove the KDP barcode?

Most paperback books need a barcode for print and distribution. If KDP is placing the barcode automatically, leave the barcode area clear instead of trying to remove it.

### Can artwork go behind the barcode?

Simple background color or subtle texture can usually go behind the barcode. Important text, logos, QR codes, detailed illustrations, and busy patterns should stay outside the barcode area.

### Why did KDP suddenly add a white barcode box?

KDP adds the white box so the barcode is readable on the printed cover. If your design has content in that area, the box can cover it or trigger a warning.

### How much space should I leave for the barcode?

Use the barcode area shown in the latest KDP template and leave extra padding around it. Do not guess from an old project or another author's cover.

### Can Canva templates cause barcode problems?

Yes. Canva templates often ignore KDP production zones. Import the KDP template as a locked guide layer and keep text, logos, QR codes, and borders outside the barcode box.

### Does hardcover KDP use the same barcode placement?

Not always. Hardcover templates can have different layout requirements. Generate the correct template for the exact format and setup.

### Can I put social media handles near the barcode?

Avoid it. Social handles, websites, and QR codes are important information. Place them away from the lower-right barcode zone.

### Will KDP reject my book if text overlaps the barcode?

KDP may warn or reject the cover. Even if it passes, the printed barcode box can cover your text, so it is better to fix the layout before publishing.

## Final Check Before You Upload Again

Barcode warnings are frustrating because the design often looks finished before upload. But the fix is usually simple: respect the reserved barcode zone, move important content away, keep the background clean, and export a fresh print-ready PDF.
